BLOCKER: `design_pack.evaluate(item_id)` returns `[]` whenever the lookup yields nothing (`get_epic(...) or {}`), so an unknown/renamed item id, store mismatch, or empty record silently disables design-pack enforcement at Gate 1 instead of failing closed.
MAJOR: Fail-open remains on parse: malformed or non-ISO `created_at`/`enforce_from` (e.g. `2026/10/05`, missing month leading zero, unexpected suffix after slicing `[:10]`) hits `except ValueError: return False`, skipping enforcement with no warning surfaced to the gate output.

The missing-`created_at` guard for `in_progress` items was added only to `main()`'s batch scan, not to `check()`/`evaluate()`; a per-item Gate 1 run on an in-progress item with no `created_at` still returns `[]` and passes, so the two enforcement paths disagree.

No new tests cover `evaluate()`, the `date.fromisoformat` fallback, or the `in_progress`-without-`created_at` finding; the only test change asserts a section-title rename, leaving the enforcement logic unverified.
MINOR: `evaluate()` re-enters the backlog directly (`backlog.get_epic("product_forge", None, item_id)`) while `gate1_check` previously used `ar._get_item`; two different item-resolution paths can diverge on tenant/scope defaults.

Renaming section 10 to "Trail metrics (per stage)" and replacing the numbered cross-reference with a prose pointer means any other parser/doc/test keying on "## 10. Gate metrics" or "section 10" silently breaks; no repo-wide reference updates appear in the diff.
`should_enforce` now silently returns `False` when `enforce_from` is unset or invalid, i.e. a broken enforcement config disables the gate with no diagnostic emitted anywhere.
NIT: `from datetime import date` is imported inside `should_enforce` on a hot check path; hoist to module level alongside the other imports.
The `main()` `created_at` check appends a bare item-level message without the `: ` severity/context prefix used by surrounding problems, making mixed output inconsistent to parse.
SUMMARY: Overall the diff is a narrow, well-scoped cleanup (API extraction, date parsing, section rename), but the enforcement entry point is fail-open: unknown items, malformed dates, and missing `enforce_from` all resolve to "not enforced" with no signal, and Gate 1 lacks the in-progress `created_at` guard that only the batch scan has.
Top risks: silent gate bypass via lookup/parse failures, enforcement-path divergence between scan and per-item Gate 1, and zero test coverage on the new evaluation logic.
